Description:
Problem:
Agent-made commits in worktree configurations weren't correctly attributed to their originating sessions. When an agent made a commit from a sibling worktree (a different git worktree in the same repository), the system relied solely on worktree path matching to link commits to sessions. This caused commits to either lose session linkage or, in cases of leaked test fixture sessions, to incorrectly link to the wrong session—producing dangling or malformed checkpoint trailers. The root issue: process identity wasn't being tracked, so there was no way to attribute a commit to the specific agent that made it across worktree boundaries.
Solution:
The branch introduces process-identity-based commit attribution that records the agent process's identity (PID + start time) at session start, then matches it at commit time to link commits to their originating sessions regardless of worktree. Key changes:
Process ancestry tracking (proctree package, new): Captures the agent process identity—the first non-shell ancestor—to guard against PID reuse and filter out shared user-side infrastructure (shells, tmux, terminal emulator, IDE).
Identity-first linking (session_identity.go, new): Commit hooks walk their ancestry and match against recorded agent processes. Nearest ancestor wins; ties go to the most recently interacting session. This makes agent commits link to their own session in any worktree without relying on path bookkeeping.
Guest-linked commits: When a commit identity-matches outside the session's home worktree, it condenses and links but preserves worktree-coupled state (BaseCommit, shadow-branch realignment) on the session's home worktree only.
Fallback worktree matching: Commits with no recorded agent in their ancestry (human commits) continue to use worktree-path matching, now with liveness filtering to resolve ambiguity across multiple worktrees.
Test isolation safeguards: Session state store now refuses to open outside the temp root under go test, failing loudly when tests lack proper repo isolation to prevent fixture leaks.
Human commits remain unaffected; agent commits now link correctly across worktrees.

commit 8581735744a91586c16517a499ead6e1b3951814
Author: Peyton Montei <peyton@entire.io>
Date:   Mon Aug 17 17:09:51 2026 -0700

    refactor(strategy): converge identity linking on proclive, delete proctree
    
    Trail review (1061) found internal/proctree duplicating the existing
    proclive package: same ancestry walk, same per-platform introspection
    (one sysctl/stat parse apart), and — decisively — proclive's Identity is
    already persisted on EVERY turn start as SessionState.Owner by
    captureSessionOwner, seven lines from where this branch re-walked the
    same process tree into a second field. The review also showed the
    duplicate's Windows walker ran in no CI job (the Windows job filters on
    test names carrying Windows/MSYS; none did), had an orphan-reparenting
    hazard PID recycling makes real, cost one process-table snapshot per
    ancestry level, and that the shell filter was missing "entire" and "go"
    — both already on proclive's transient list.
    
    Converge instead of duplicating:
    
    - proclive gains HasAncestor(Identity) — the commit-attribution
      question ("was this process spawned, however indirectly, by the
      recorded owner?") with proclive's host, boot, and start-fingerprint
      guards, so a recycled PID or an identity recorded on another machine
      can never match — two guards the deleted package lacked (its own doc
      conceded the Linux cross-reboot collision that proclive's bootID
      closes). Plus IdentityOf(pid) for callers and tests.
    - findSessionByCommitAncestry matches SessionState.Owner via
      HasAncestor. No new recording, no AgentAncestry field, no
      refreshAgentAncestry (Owner is re-captured every turn start, which
      already covers resume under a new agent process). Ties — one agent
      process hosting several sessions, or a nested agent whose outer agent
      is also an ancestor — go to the most recently interacting session.
    - internal/proctree is deleted. On platforms proclive cannot introspect
      (Windows), identity matching reports nothing and linking falls back
      to worktree matching — honestly, rather than via platform code no CI
      job executed.
    
    This also positions PR #1777 (cross-common-dir auto-adopt): its
    owner-matching compares first-non-transient identities and breaks when
    a non-transient wrapper interposes at commit time; HasAncestor's
    any-ancestor semantics are immune and reusable there.

+**Identity matching**: reuses the owner fingerprint liveness already
+records — `SessionState.Owner`, a `proclive.Identity` captured on every turn
+start by `captureSessionOwner` (the first non-transient ancestor of the hook:
+agents run hooks as children, possibly via `sh -c`, and proclive skips
+shells, the `entire` binary itself, and the Go toolchain). At commit time the
+hook snapshots its ancestry once (`proclive.CurrentAncestry`) and asks
+`Ancestry.Depth(owner)` per candidate: was this commit's process spawned,
+however indirectly, by that session's agent? Snapshotting once matters — the
+shared store holds one state file per session, so a per-candidate walk would
+repeat the hostname, boot-id, and proc reads dozens of times per commit.
+Host, boot, and start-time guards mean a recycled PID or an identity recorded
+on another machine can never match. The nearest ancestor wins, so a nested
+agent is attributed over the outer agent that spawned it; only sessions
+matching at the same depth (one agent process hosting several sessions) fall
+back to the most recently interacting one. On platforms proclive cannot introspect (Windows),
+identity matching reports nothing and linking falls back to worktree
+matching. This makes an agent-made commit link to
+its own session **in any worktree**, with no bookkeeping to drift. A commit
+identity-matched outside the session's home worktree is **guest-linked**: it
+condenses and links, but never mutates worktree-coupled state (`BaseCommit`,
+shadow-branch realignment) — those follow only the session's own worktree HEAD.
+
+**Worktree matching** (always computed; the sole mechanism for commits with
+no recorded agent in their ancestry — human commits, detached runners): exact
+`WorktreePath` match first, then sessions from a sibling worktree of the same
+repo, provided they resolve to a single worktree. Imported sessions (`Kind=imported`) never link —
+they are historical records. When candidates span several worktrees, sessions
+that interacted within the last 15 minutes are preferred; if a single live
+worktree remains it links, otherwise the hook declines with a stderr hint
+naming `entire session adopt` (two genuinely live sessions in different
+worktrees are never guessed between).
+
+Under `go test`, the session state store refuses to open outside the temp
+root (both `session.NewStateStore` and `NewStateStoreForWorktree`), so a test
+missing repo isolation fails loudly instead of leaking fixture sessions into
+a real repo's `.git/entire-sessions` — leaked fixtures once hijacked commit
+linking and produced a dangling `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer.

I read all three branches, built and ran the affected package tests locally on each, and confirmed all three PRs are green on CI (#2013, #2015, #2029).

---

## 1061 — `feat(strategy): link commits to sessions by process identity` (#2013)

The core design is right: union-not-precedence between worktree and identity matching, nearest-ancestor-wins, host/boot/start-time guards, one ancestry snapshot per commit instead of per candidate. Deleting `internal/proctree` in favour of `proclive` was the correct call — `SessionState.Owner` was already being captured on every turn start seven lines away. Docs are unusually good.

**1. The guest path retains the shadow branch but still resets the checkpoint window** — `manual_commit_hooks.go:1416-1444`

The guest branch calls `resetCheckpointWindow(state)` (which sets `StepCount = 0`) and then returns *before* `shadowBranchesToDelete[shadowBranchName]` and before advancing `BaseCommit`. Two consequences:

- `CondenseSession` recomputes the shadow branch from `state.BaseCommit` + `state.WorktreeID` and reads the branch **tip tree**. Since the guest condense neither deletes the branch nor moves `BaseCommit`, the same shadow content stays eligible to be condensed again into the next checkpoint this session links to. The home path avoids this precisely by deleting the branch and advancing `BaseCommit` to a new branch name.
- `StepCount == 0` un-pins the branch. `cleanupShadowBranchIfUnused` (`manual_commit_condensation.go:1471`) and `doctor.go:690` both gate on `state.StepCount > 0` to decide "another session still needs this branch", and `isWarnableStaleEndedSession` / `classifySession` (`doctor.go:289`) both bail on `StepCount <= 0`. So between a guest condense and the session's next `SaveStep`, a concurrent session sharing the branch can delete it, and if the session ends in that window its shadow branch is orphaned without doctor flagging it.

The comment justifies retaining the branch by the carry-forward hazard — but carry-forward is already gated separately by `isSessionHomeWorktree(repoDir, state)` at line 1327. So the retention looks like belt-and-braces that now contradicts the `StepCount` reset. Either skip `resetCheckpointWindow` for guests, or schedule the branch for deletion (its content just landed in the guest checkpoint).

**2. `condenseAndUpdateState`'s variadic makes "guest" the default** — line 1428

```go
var isHome bool
if len(opts) > 0 { isHome = isSessionHomeWorktree(opts[0].repoDir, state) }
```

Both current callers pass `condenseOpts`, so this is latent — but a caller that omits it silently gets guest treatment (no branch cleanup, no `BaseCommit` advance, `FilesTouched` never cleared). For a variadic that's the wrong fail-safe direction. Make `repoDir` a positional parameter, or default `isHome = true`.

**3. `isSessionHomeWorktree` uses raw `==` on paths** — `session_identity.go:121`

`reconcileWorktreePathForResumedTurn` in the same package compares worktree paths with `filepath.Clean`. In practice both sides come from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` so they agree today, but path equality now gates *state mutation* rather than just matching, so the failure mode of a mismatch is worse than it was. Cheap to harden.

**4. The ambiguity hint can fire once per replayed commit during a rebase** — `session_identity.go:44`

The stderr hint lives inside `findSessionsForCommitLinking`, which `PostCommit` also calls. `PostCommit` resolves the trailer first and only computes `isRebase := isGitSequenceOperation(ctx)` *after* the find, so a `git rebase` replaying N trailer-bearing commits in a worktree with ambiguous sessions prints the hint N times. Suppressing it when `isGitSequenceOperation` is true, or only emitting from `PrepareCommitMsg`, would fix it.

**5. Test coverage stops short of the riskiest code.** `session_identity_test.go` covers the matcher, the union, imported exclusion, ambiguity/liveness and `updateBaseCommitIfChanged` gating — but nothing exercises the guest branch of `condenseAndUpdateState` or the carry-forward gate, which is where the "would replace the home worktree's in-flight state with foreign files" hazard the comments describe actually lives.

Two things worth stating in the PR description rather than fixing:

- The guest gate is **path-based, not identity-based**, so it also changes the pre-existing cross-worktree *fallback* path. That's an improvement (the fallback used to rewrite `BaseCommit` from a foreign worktree and orphan the home shadow branch), but the docs frame guest-linking as identity-only, and this is the behaviour change most likely to surface in existing repos.
- `resolveWorktreeCandidates` now links where the old code declined: one live worktree within 15 minutes wins. Two live worktrees where one is mid-long-build (>15 min idle) now silently links to the other. Reasonable trade for #1852, but it's a guess the previous code refused to make, and `recentSessionWindow` should be called out as the knob it is.

---

## 1064 — `fix(doctor): hint --force instead of crashing` (#2015)

Clean, and correctly modelled on the existing `checkGitHooks` degrade — same guard, same wording, same "return nil" semantics. It reuses `canCondenseStuckSession` for the hint rather than re-deriving it, so the disclosed fix can't drift from what `--force` actually does. Nothing blocking. Three small things:

- `confirmDoctorFix` got an internal safety net; `promptSessionAction` didn't. That asymmetry is the one thing a future call site could trip over — worth either adding the same guard or a comment saying why it isn't needed.
- Non-interactive runs still exit 0 with stuck sessions reported. Consistent with `checkGitHooks`, so presumably deliberate — but if anyone wants `entire doctor` usable as a CI gate, now is when to say so.
- Tests only cover the non-interactive path (the `go test` default). That matches repo norms; just noting the interactive branch has no pin.

---

## 1073 — `feat: self-heal zombie sessions via detached sweep` (#2029)

**1. The predicate never nominates IDLE dead-owner sessions — the case the design calls the common one** — `session_sweep.go:36`

```go
if st.Phase.IsActive() { return st.OwnerExited() }
```

`Phase.IsActive()` is `p == PhaseActive` only (`session/phase.go:47`). An IDLE state falls through the imported check to `st.Phase != session.PhaseEnded → return false`. But `runSessionSweep`'s first action is `finalizeExitedSessions(ctx, states)`, which keys on `OwnerExited()` and *does* cover IDLE. So the sweep can fix IDLE zombies but will never be spawned for a repo whose only zombies are IDLE.

CLAUDE.md is explicit about this being the case that matters: "**`OwnerExited` deliberately covers IDLE as well as ACTIVE** — an agent that finishes its last turn and then quits leaves IDLE, so gating on ACTIVE alone missed the common case." The new doc paragraph asserts the opposite — "IDLE sessions with a dead owner are out of scope, matching doctor's boundary" — and that justification doesn't hold: `entire doctor` calls the same `finalizeExitedSessions`, so doctor's boundary *includes* IDLE. Fix is one line: `if !st.IsEnded() { return st.OwnerExited() }`.

Relatedly, the `"idle session is never a zombie"` test case has no `Owner` at all, so `OwnerExited()` is false regardless of phase — it doesn't exercise the case its name claims.

**2. The detached sweep inherits a budget whose whole rationale is an interactive caller** — `session_finalize.go:15-31`

`sweepCondenseBudget = 1 * time.Second`, justified in its own doc comment by "the callers here are interactive commands — including `entire status --json` ... where nothing prints until the sweep returns." `__sweep_sessions` exists precisely so nobody is waiting, yet it gets the same 1s cap, and the 15-minute spawn throttle sits on top. A post-upgrade backlog therefore drains at roughly 1s of condensing per 15 minutes — which undercuts the feature's headline claim. Parameterize the budget for the detached path, or say in the PR why 1s is still right there.

**3. Throttle failure mode is "spawn every time"** — `session_sweep.go:236`

```go
if commonDir, cerr := session.GetGitCommonDir(ctx); cerr == nil && sweepRecentlySpawned(commonDir, time.Now()) { return }
```

A `GetGitCommonDir` error skips the throttle entirely — one detached child per session start, which is exactly what the throttle exists to prevent. `recentlySpawnedMarker`'s "never worse than before this guard existed" is true for the trail refresh but understates it here, where the guard is the only thing bounding fork count.

**4. The O(N) work happens before the throttle check.** Every session start reads every state file in the shared dir and runs a `proclive` probe per ACTIVE session, then checks the throttle. Reordering isn't free — `recentlySpawnedMarker` *records* on a miss, so a read-only variant would be needed first — but the current ordering deserves a comment saying it's deliberate, given this repo's open hook-latency floor.

Things done well and worth keeping: the condense-only contract with the explicit "discards are doctor's" boundary, the imported-session guard (with the reason spelled out), the re-load-and-re-check under the lock before acting, `IsCondensableEndedSession`'s note that it's a re-check for PostCommit but the *primary* check for the sweep, and `ensureLogger` + logging the top-level error in the detached child.

---

## Cross-cutting

- **1061 and 1073 merge cleanly except for one docs conflict**: both insert a paragraph at the same anchor in `docs/architecture/sessions-and-checkpoints.md`. All Go files auto-merge. Whichever lands second just needs the doc rebase.
- **`SessionState.Owner` is becoming a single point of failure for three behaviours**: liveness (already shipped), commit attribution (1061), and background sweeping (1073). It's nil on Windows and whenever hook ancestry resolves to only transient processes. Do we have any signal on how often `ResolveOwner` actually succeeds across the supported agents? Both PRs degrade correctly when it's nil, but the value of both features is proportional to a resolve rate nobody has measured.
- 1061's `ensureTestIsolatedStateDir` hard-fails `session.NewStateStore` under `go test` outside the temp root. That's the right call and CI is green, but it raises the bar for every future test touching session state — worth a line in the PR so it isn't discovered as a mystery failure.

content.text:
Re-reviewed both at their new tips. All nine findings are genuinely fixed — I verified each by reading the diff and running the tests, plus a mutation probe on the one that mattered most.

## 1061 (#2013) — tip `9fc73e026`

| Finding | Fix | Verified |
|---|---|---|
| StepCount pin | `pendingStepCount` restored after `resetCheckpointWindow` | Reverted the two lines → `TestPostCommit_GuestCondensationPreservesHomeShadowState` fails on the StepCount assertion, and the log confirms the guest condense ran. Non-vacuous. |
| Variadic `opts` | now positional `opts condenseOpts` | builds, single call site each |
| Raw `==` on paths | `filepath.Clean` both sides + `TestIsSessionHomeWorktree_CleansPaths` | pass |
| Rebase hint spam | `&& !isGitSequenceOperation(ctx)` + a `.git/rebase-merge` fixture test | pass |
| Test coverage gap | `TestPostCommit_GuestCondensationPreservesHomeShadowState` — end-to-end, asserts the shadow ref is byte-identical | pass |
| Both scope notes | landed in CLAUDE.md, the arch doc, **and** the `recentSessionWindow` constant comment | — |

**One correction to my own review.** I claimed the guest path re-condenses the same shadow content. That was wrong. `cpkg.WriteOptions` carries `FilesTouched` (names), the transcript, prompts and tasks — not the shadow tree's blobs — so a guest condense genuinely does not consume the home worktree's shadow content. Peyton's comment ("the checkpoint window was consumed, but the home worktree's shadow content was not") is accurate, and preserving the pin was the right fix rather than deleting the branch.

**One new, low observation.** `ef2deecf6` inverted `isSessionHomeWorktree` so an unknown path is now "not home". Right default for mutation safety, but a session with an empty `WorktreePath` that identity matching finds is now permanently a guest — `BaseCommit` frozen, shadow branch never released, `FilesTouched` never cleared, so it re-condenses on every commit — and it happens silently. `findSessionByCommitAncestry` is the only route in (the worktree fallback already does `if state.WorktreePath == "" { continue }`), so skipping empty-`WorktreePath` states there too would close it. Reachability is genuinely low — every current writer sets the field, so this is legacy state files only.

## 1073 (#2029) — tip `f4881a3c3`

| Finding | Fix | Verified |
|---|---|---|
| IDLE scoping | `if !st.IsEnded() { return st.OwnerExited() }` — exactly the shape `finalizeExitedSessions` uses | test fixture now carries `deadOwner` and asserts `want: true`; the false "matching doctor's boundary" doc line is gone |
| Condense budget | `finalizeExitedSessions(ctx, states, condenseDeadline)`; sweep passes `time.Time{}`, status/doctor pass `interactiveSweepCondenseBudget`. `endSessionNow` already treats zero as unbounded (`!condenseDeadline.IsZero()`), and the scanner-failure path still forces `time.Now()` to skip | tests pass |
| Throttle fail-open | resolves the common dir first and returns on error; added a `sweepGitCommonDir` seam and a test asserting zero spawns; my secondary point about the discovery/throttle ordering is now an explicit comment naming the read-only-marker prerequisite | pass |

They also went past the findings: imported sessions are now excluded from `finalizeExitedSessions` itself (`isExitedSessionFinalizationCandidate`), and `f4881a3c3` aligned the predicate with `IsCondensableEndedSession` on `(StepCount <= 0 && !HasTaskContent())`.

**Two new, low observations:**

1. `session_sweep.go:46` — after `if !st.IsEnded() { … }` three lines above, `st.Phase != session.PhaseEnded` can only be true for the half-ended shape (`EndedAt` set, `Phase` still IDLE) that `IsEnded`'s own doc exists to normalize — "a state file can carry one without the other (a legacy record, or a partial write)". Such a state is dropped here, skipped by `finalizeExitedSessions` (because `OwnerExited` returns false once `IsEnded`), and falls into `classifySession`'s `default: return nil`. So it's invisible to both sweep halves *and* doctor, and only the 7-day purge reaches it — which deletes rather than condenses. The function now contradicts itself on exactly the case it just started getting right.

2. `proclive.Check` re-reads `os.Hostname()` and `bootID()` per identity, with no memoization — on Linux that's a `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id` read plus a `/proc/<pid>/stat` read every call. Widening the candidate set from ACTIVE to all non-ended is correct, but it also widened this: in my clone that's **33** `Check` calls per session start, up from 3. Sub-millisecond each, so not a blocker — but it's now on the hook path, it scales with the state-file count (which grows to the 7-day threshold), and `proclive` already has the right pattern in `CurrentAncestry` (resolve host/boot once, match in memory). A `Prober`/`CheckAll` would mirror it.

## Status

Both merge cleanly except the same one docs hunk in `sessions-and-checkpoints.md` (both still insert at the same anchor). All CI green on both; the only failing check is `Entire Gates`, and its detail is `Approvals: failed — No reviewers have approved this trail` — Checks and Findings both pass.

Yes, I think it's the right call — with two qualifications.

**Why merging now is right.** None of the three remaining findings is a regression against main. Two are only reachable through legacy state files (an empty `WorktreePath`, or an `EndedAt`-without-`PhaseEnded` partial write) that no current writer can produce, and the third is pure perf. Both PRs are well-tested — I mutation-probed the guest-condensation test and it genuinely fails when the fix is reverted, which is more than most tests in this area can claim. Holding two reviewed, green PRs on legacy-only edge cases would be the wrong trade.

**Qualification 1: don't merge them back-to-back.** Land 1061, give it a few days of dogfooding, then 1073. Not ritual caution — 1061 changes commit→session attribution for *every* commit in *every* repo, and the failure mode is a wrong or dangling checkpoint trailer, which is precisely the bug class this repo has been chasing. If something's off you want one suspect, not two. You also get the conflict resolution for free: 1073 has to take a main merge and resolve that docs hunk anyway once 1061 lands.

**Qualification 2: trim the follow-up to two fixes, not three.** The two one-liners are worth doing (`isSessionHomeWorktree` skipping empty-`WorktreePath` states at the identity matcher, and `isSweepableZombie:46` not silently dropping the half-ended shape). The `proclive.Check` memoization I'd leave as a comment on the code, not a change — it's a few hundred microseconds against an open ~3-second p50 hook-latency floor. Fixing it now is optimising the wrong end.

**The thing actually worth doing instead** is the `Owner` resolve-rate question from my 1073 comment, which nobody has answered. Both features are load-bearing on a field that's nil on Windows and nil whenever hook ancestry resolves to only transient processes — and if it resolves poorly on some agent, that agent silently gets none of this. I have one data point from measuring my own clone while reviewing: **33 of 34 non-ended sessions carry an `Owner`**. Encouraging, but that's one machine with a Claude Code-heavy mix. A short script across a few teammates' state dirs, bucketed by `agent_type`, would tell you whether these two PRs are load-bearing or decorative for Cursor, Codex, Copilot CLI and Droid. ## Problem

A session state can carry `EndedAt` without `PhaseEnded`. `State.IsEnded` exists for exactly that shape, and its doc names it:

> Both halves matter and neither implies the other in practice: Phase is what the state machine sets, EndedAt is what the finalizing write stamps, and a state file can carry one without the other (a legacy record, or a partial write). Callers that filter for active sessions must agree on this rule, so it lives here rather than being re-spelled at each site.

The sweep re-spelled it, and its two halves ended up disagreeing. `isSweepableZombie` correctly used `IsEnded()` to route non-ended zombies to `finalizeExitedSessions`, then three lines later re-tested `Phase == PhaseEnded` before nominating a condense.

For a half-ended state, **both halves declined**:

- `finalizeExitedSessions` skips it, because `OwnerExited()` returns false once `IsEnded()`.
- the condense path skipped it on the phase test.

`entire doctor` does not reach it either — `classifySession`’s phase switch falls through to `default: return nil`. So the only thing that ever touched such a session was the 7-day stale purge, which **deletes** the uncondensed content rather than condensing it.

## Fix

Three gates had to move together, and each is independently load-bearing — reverting any one alone fails the new end-to-end test (verified, see below):

| Gate | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `isSweepableZombie` | Drop the `Phase` re-test. Reaching that line already means `IsEnded()`, so the test could only ever exclude the half-ended shape. |
| `runSessionSweep` | Both loop guards keyed on `Phase`, so a nominated half-ended session was skipped before *and* after the fresh re-load. |
| `IsCondensableEndedSession` | Same `Phase` test, so a session that survived both guards was still reported non-condensable. |

## Blast radius

`IsCondensableEndedSession` is shared with the PostCommit stale-session warning, which now also counts half-ended sessions holding uncondensed content. That is the same correction, not a side effect: they are stale and actionable by doctor for the same reason a `PhaseEnded` one is.

## Deliberately not changed

`doctor`’s `classifySession` has the same phase-switch gap, so a half-ended session is still not listed by `entire doctor`. It is a separate command on a separate path, and the sweep now condenses these before doctor would have to. Happy to fold it in if you would rather have the two consistent.

## Verification

`TestRunSessionSweep_CondensesHalfEndedSession` builds the shape end to end (`Phase: PhaseIdle`, `EndedAt` 48h old, `StepCount: 2`, shadow ref present) and asserts the sweep actually condensed it — not merely that the predicate stopped matching. Mutation-probed all three gates:

```
revert isSweepableZombie          -> FAIL "a half-ended session with uncondensed steps must nominate the sweep"
revert runSessionSweep guards     -> FAIL "the half-ended session must no longer hold uncondensed content"
revert IsCondensableEndedSession  -> FAIL "the sweep must have condensed the half-ended session, not just skipped it"
```
